title: False Kamani: Ancient False Kamani Trees You Can Visit
meta_description: The tropical almond with a flat fan of branches. Okinawa's was planted by officials about 200 years ago, and Hilo's stands at a church corner.
intro: False kamani, the tropical almond, is a spreading tree of the Pacific coasts, planted for the wide, low shade of its flat tiers of branches. Ours begin in Okinawa, where a tree at Tomari was planted around two hundred years ago by officials sent from the Ryukyu government at Shuri, as a parting gift to the villagers they had befriended. It is 3.7 metres round and about 11.5 metres tall, and it stands beside a national highway. In Hilo, the tree at Haili and Ululani Streets is called kamani by the local newspaper, which gave it 194 years in 2014, though the true kamani is a different species. And in Florianopolis, a reader found one on the shore at Ribeirao da Ilha, its limbs running almost level over the water, with two plaques fixed to its trunk.
